title: Navigating Divorce: 401k Match vs Paying Off Loans
body: I just went through a divorce at 52 and I'm trying to figure out what to do with my finances. My company matches 5% of my 401k contributions but I also have some high-interest debt that's been weighing on me. I feel like paying off the loans would give me peace of mind, but should I be prioritizing retirement savings? Any advice from those who've gone through similar situations?

title: Temporary fencing for a new pasture on a tight budget.
body: I just set up my first small pasture here in Bozeman and I'm sharing a trick that saved me from buying new fencing. Instead of putting up permanent posts, I used 6' T-posts with a few strands of barbed wire to create a temporary fence around the area. It's easy to move them around as the grass grows in and it only took a few hours to set up.

title: Avoiding Lifestyle Creep After My Raise
body: I was lucky enough to get a 10% raise when I retired from teaching. At first, my wife and I thought we'd treat ourselves to a new RV, but then we remembered all the frugal habits we learned over the years. We decided to keep our spending in check by taking more weekend trips on our old car instead of making big purchases. It's been 5 years now and I'm proud to say we've stuck to it.

title: My 2 Cents on Modern Farming Practices
body: I've been fixing tractors for years and I gotta say, I'm still amazed at how many farmers are relying on those fancy precision planters. Don't get me wrong, they're great and all, but sometimes I think we forget what made our grandfathers' farms so successful - hard work and good ol' fashioned instinct. A little rain can go a long way in figuring out when to plant.

title: Streaming service fatigue is real
body: I'm at my wit's end trying to keep track of multiple subscriptions. My kid wants to watch something on Netflix, but I don't want to pay for it. So we switch to Hulu and then they can't find the show they want. We have Disney+, Apple TV+ and Amazon Prime too. It's exhausting trying to manage all these services and their menus are always changing.

title: Overcoming the struggle of building a first emergency fund as a nurse on night shifts
body: I've been working towards saving for an emergency fund since I started my nursing career. The challenge is juggling irregular schedules, physical demands and high stress levels with budgeting. After 2 years, I finally reached my goal of saving $5k in an easily accessible savings account. It's been a mental game, but being prepared has given me peace of mind on nights when things get tough.
